To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of components of the PA-system and integrins is associated with the metastatic capacity of human melanoma cells and that these components are also expressed in advanced primary melanoma lesions.
metastasizing human melanocytes show increased expression and function of uPA and PAI-2 and increased expression and function integrins VLA-2, VLA-6, and VLA-5.

metastasizing human melanomas are characterized by increased expression of uPA and PAI-2 and increased expression of VLA-1, VLA-2, VLA-6, and α5β1 integrins, and by a higher degree of activation of the integrins involved, compared to nonmetastaszing human melanomas and normal melanocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecules involved in the metastatic process of human melanomas and the elucidation of their role in this process.
the expression and function in melanoma cells of components of the PA-system and integrins.
the identification of proteins involved in tumor progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the metastatic phenotype in human melanoma is characterized by an elevated expression of components of the uPA-system and of integrin receptors, resulting in increased proteolytic activity and adhesion to extracellular matrix.
the highly metastatic melanoma cell line expresses higher levels of proteolytic enzymes and adhesion molecules than the nonmetastatic cell lines.
the expression of uPA and uPA inhibitors, as well as of VLA-6, VLA-2, and VLA-3, is related to the invasive and metastatic potential of human melanoma cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression and function (in terms of cell adhesion) of the components of the plamogen activator system and of integrins involved, are different between metastatic and nonmetastastatic melanoma.

the highly invasive and highly metastatic melanoma cell line M21 expresses components of both the PA system and integrins involved in cell-matrix adhesion, which are absent in the nonmetastatic cell lines and normal cultured melanocytes.

metastasizing melanoma cells have a more invasive and aggressive phenotype, as reflected by the expression of components of the PA and adhesion system, which is also reflected by the expression pattern in fresh human melanoma lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differences in expression of proteases and integrins between metastasizing versus nonmetastasising melanoma cell lines can be used to identify molecules involved in tumor cell invasion.
the components of the plasmogen activator system and the integrins involved are important in melanoma invasion and metastasis.
differences in expression of proteases, their inhibitors, and cell adhesion molecules are associated with the invasive and metastatic behavior of human melanoma cells.
